requirements.statement: A conversation with at least one run offers 'Trace of this conversation' in its menu, and the Traces view narrowed to one conversation offers to open that conversation as one trace; both open the same view of that conversation.

The view shows every run of the conversation as a numbered turn, in the order the runs started, each placed on one time axis shared by all turns, with its start time, its cost when priced, 'from you' when the operator started it, and its duration; a turn still running is drawn open and grows.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06: a conversation that spans a night drawn to scale is slivers; folding keeps every turn readable.
requirements.statement: A stretch longer than 20 minutes in which no turn of the conversation was running is drawn as a break of fixed width, marked across every row and labelled in the axis with its length; turns and shorter gaps are drawn to scale; axis labels that would overlap are left out of the drawing and kept in the hover text of their tick or break.

requirements.rationale: On the conversation's axis a ten-minute turn of a day-long conversation is a sliver, and its spans would be invisible (seen in the mock, 2026-11-06).
requirements.statement: A turn unfolds to show its spans as the single-run trace shows them (nested, named, coloured by kind), drawn across that turn's own duration rather than the conversation's axis, with a line saying so; selecting a turn or a span shows its detail below the timeline.

The operator narrows the view to a range of turns (from one turn to another) and to turns that started within the last 24 hours, 6 hours or hour, or at any time; the timeline, its breaks and the totals are redrawn over the turns that remain, a narrowed view offers to show every turn again, and a narrowing that leaves no turn says so.

Above the timeline the view totals the turns shown: how many of the conversation's turns, the time they were running and the time from the first one's start to the last one's end, their cost with the count of unpriced turns left out, their errors as failed turns and tool errors, and their model calls, tool calls and time waiting on the operator.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06: each conversation's trace keeps a clear boundary; a chain of carry-overs would otherwise grow without limit.
requirements.statement: The trace of a conversation carried over from an earlier one shows only its own turns, names the conversation it continued, and opens that conversation's trace from there.

requirements.rationale: A conversation of 24 turns can hold over 10,000 spans; the turn rows answer most questions without them.
requirements.statement: Opening the view reads the conversation's turn rows and totals without reading every turn's spans; a turn's spans are read when it is first unfolded, and a turn whose trace was cleared or never recorded unfolds to a line saying it has no trace.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02, after driving the mock: 'lives inside Activity'.
requirements.statement: The Activity tab has a Traces view for the selected project, beside Ledger, Activity and Logs, which the operator reaches without going through Settings.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: agents by default, and the Hub's internals behind a quieter choice. About 1,170 of the operator's traces are runs, beside tens of thousands of the Hub's own; unfiltered, the runs are buried.
requirements.statement: The traces view opens showing agents' runs only. The Hub's own traces (worker calls, requests, background work, events) are reached through a separate 'Hub internals' choice that is less prominent than the filters on runs, and appear only once one of them is chosen.
The traces view can be filtered by agent, conversation, task, run, kind and time range, any of them together, and the list and the statistics both show only what matches every filter in force.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02. Six tasks behind runs on the operator's Hub no longer exist; the mock showed one as 'task-b9bf0f35c2c5'.
requirements.statement: Each listed run shows its agent, model, task (its reference and title, when it worked one) or the conversation it was a turn of, when it started, how long it took, what it cost, and whether it counts as an error. A task with no reference and no title is shown as a task that no longer exists, never by its raw id.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: switchable grouping.
requirements.statement: The filtered traces can be grouped by agent, model, task, conversation, kind or day, switchable from the view, and each group shows how many traces it holds and its statistics.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: cost, duration and errors are what they want to see most; cancelled and interrupted runs count as errors, routine failed tool calls inside a finished run do not. On the operator's Hub runs are completed 1,211, failed 12, stopped 5, running 3.
requirements.statement: The view shows, over everything the current filter matches and for each group, the total cost, the total and average duration, and the number of errors, and these three are shown before any other statistic. A run counts as an error when it failed, when it was stopped (cancelled or interrupted), or when its trace ended in error; a run that completed with a failed tool call inside it does not.
The view also offers, less prominently, token counts, the number of model calls and tool calls, and time spent waiting for a permission or an answer, over the same filter and groups.

requirements.rationale: The list is paged (the Settings list shows 10 at a time); totals over one page would understate cost and errors without saying so.
requirements.statement: The statistics count every trace the filter matches, not only the page of rows currently loaded.

requirements.rationale: Driving the mock, a click in the middle of a row landed on its task and filtered instead of opening the run.
requirements.statement: Choosing a listed trace opens it in the existing trace view, and closing it returns to the traces view with the same filters and grouping. Narrowing to a row's task or conversation is a control of its own, so choosing the row anywhere else opens its trace.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: check every screen a trace can be reached from; the task story's run row already does this and is the model.
requirements.statement: Every screen that names or lists a specific agent run offers that run's trace, and following it opens that run's trace, not another run's or a list.

requirements.rationale: The per-turn link is faint and the 'Trace of the last turn' menu item exists but is never shown (ConversationBar.tsx:201).
requirements.statement: From a conversation, the operator opens the trace of its most recent run from the conversation's own controls, without finding the per-turn link, and each turn's own trace link stays.
A run count shown elsewhere (a build's runs, a task's runs, the project's work summary) opens the traces view filtered to exactly those runs.
On the operator's Hub (about 137k spans, 1,170 runs on 2026-11-02), the traces view's default list and statistics appear within 2 seconds.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02. 16 finished runs on the operator's Hub have no measured cost; counting them as zero would make a total look complete when it is not. The project's model record already reports them this way. A running run has not reported its cost yet, which is not the same as the Hub failing to measure it (found driving the mock).
requirements.statement: A finished run whose cost the Hub could not measure is shown as unpriced, never as a zero cost, and a cost total that leaves such runs out says how many it left out. A run still running is shown with no cost yet and is not counted as unpriced.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-02: one place to look for traces.
requirements.statement: Project Settings' traces section no longer lists traces itself; in place of its 'Recent traces' list it links to the traces view in Activity. Retention, export to a collector, download and clearing stay where they are.

requirements.rationale: trace-D4: all mutating, all agent-credential, all errors and slow requests.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL record a project's API request as an `aw.request` span carrying its method, route template, status code, duration, actor and project when the request is not a GET or HEAD, was made with a run credential, answered 4xx or 5xx, or took longer than one second.

requirements.rationale: trace-D4: the app's routine read polling and the SSE stream are skipped by default, behind a setting.
requirements.statement: The operator's other GET and HEAD requests and the SSE stream SHALL NOT be recorded unless the project's trace settings turn `record_reads` on, in which case they SHALL be.

requirements.rationale: APPROVALS 2026-10-19 scope 1: an agent's calls into the Hub nest under the tool call that made them.
requirements.statement: A request made with a run's credential SHALL be a span in that run's trace, parented under the run's newest unended `execute_tool` span, or under the run's root when none is open.

requirements.rationale: APPROVALS 2026-10-19 scope 2; persist_event is the one writer of event_logs.
requirements.statement: Every event `persist_event` records SHALL appear in a trace: as a span event on the current span when there is one, else as an `aw.event` span of its own committed with the event.

requirements.rationale: APPROVALS 2026-10-19 scope 3.
requirements.statement: A job firing, a loop tick, flow and review staffing, inbound queue processing, worktree create, merge and release, task integration, a project check run, a spec fold and a distil batch SHALL each be recorded as an `aw.work` trace naming its kind.

requirements.rationale: APPROVALS 2026-10-19 scope 3: git and check commands as child spans.
requirements.statement: Each git or check command the Hub runs SHALL be an `aw.command` child span of the current trace carrying its redacted arguments, exit code and duration, with error status on a non-zero exit.

requirements.rationale: APPROVALS 2026-10-19 scope 4.
requirements.statement: A WARNING-or-higher record the Hub logs while a trace is current SHALL be stored on that trace's current span, redacted as span content is, and the download and the OTLP push SHALL carry it as an OTLP log record with its trace and span ids.

requirements.rationale: Hazard 3: the request path.
requirements.statement: Recording a request, event, background or command span SHALL NOT delay, fail or change the answer of the request or work it records; a span that cannot be written SHALL be counted as dropped.
